headline: ASX closed up 0.79% on a solid Sunday session, NRL Grand Final — Roosters vs Knights tonight at 6:30pm — is the big event of the day.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google had a strong night last session on NASDAQ, up 1.62% to $340.35 USD. The broader tech rally on NASDAQ (up 1.19%) lifted the whole sector. Analysts are still debating the Google Cloud story — revenue hit $20B but free cash flow has been scrutinised. Long-term fundamentals remain solid.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara bounced 1.37% today to $3.70, a welcome green day after a tough stretch. No specific news catalyst — likely riding a broader ASX resource sector lift. The stock is still well below your cost base, but today's move shows there's still demand for lithium exposure.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft climbed 0.92% last session to $517.53 USD — a solid move as big tech broadly rallied. Microsoft's AI products (Copilot) continue to be well received by the market, and the stock is now up 16.8% on your overall position. Nothing but good news here.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up 0.21% today, which is exactly what you'd expect from a diversified fund on a broadly positive ASX day. Steady as she goes — this one just quietly does its job.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF ticked up a modest 0.17% today. AI stocks broadly are in a holding pattern while the market debates regulation — Trump's administration is keeping AI oversight voluntary rather than mandatory, which is generally good for the sector's growth runway.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS barely moved today — up just 0.08%. It tracks the entire US share market, so last night's NASDAQ-led US rally will be better reflected in tomorrow's session. Your position is up 5.32% overall, which is a healthy return.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets dipped slightly today — down 0.16% to $94.26. No major catalyst; emerging market ETFs can be sensitive to the Aussie dollar and global risk appetite. Essentially flat on the day — don't read too much into it.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 0.44% last session to $202.73. It's still sitting at a loss of about $84 AUD overall. There's a bit of chatter in gaming circles about GTA 6's $80 price point potentially setting a new industry standard — if that sticks, it's a positive for Take-Two's revenue when GTA 6 eventually launches.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Hold through the recovery
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals bounced 1.37% today but you're still down about 45% on your position (a $67.66 AUD loss). There's no structural fix to lithium prices yet, but the long-term EV and battery storage thesis is intact. Today's green day is a small positive signal. Don't sell into this weakness — that would lock in a real loss. Sit tight and let the lithium cycle turn.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Strong position, no reason to touch it
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is your best performer at +16.8% overall, and last session added another 0.92%. The AI Copilot integration across Microsoft's product suite continues to be a growth driver. Nothing to do here — just enjoy it. Classic long-term hold.

watch_today.title: TTWO — Still underwater, but GTA 6 is the long game
watch_today.detail: Take-Two is your biggest dollar loser right now (down $83.86 AUD, -12.68%). The stock barely moved last session. The key catalyst everyone is waiting for is GTA 6 — when it launches, it's expected to be the biggest entertainment release in history. A new report suggests the $80 price point could become industry standard, which helps Take-Two's margins. If you believe in GTA 6, the thesis hasn't changed. Hold.

watch_today.title: RBA rate cut still more than a year away — budget squeeze continues
watch_today.detail: New reporting this weekend suggests the RBA won't cut rates for at least another 12 months, following the September 2026 rate hike. Mortgage holders are still under serious pressure. For your portfolio, this means the Aussie economy stays in a slow-growth phase — not ideal for domestic stocks, but your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) are unaffected.

watch_today.title: GOOG — Cloud growing, worth watching free cash flow
watch_today.detail: Google's stock rose 1.62% last night to $340.35. Analyst attention is on Google Cloud hitting $20B in revenue — impressive growth — but some analysts have flagged that free cash flow (actual cash the business generates after spending) has dropped sharply. Your position is still up 10.71% overall. No action needed, but worth keeping an eye on the next earnings report.

watch_today.title: NRL Grand Final tonight — Roosters vs Knights, 6:30pm Accor Stadium
watch_today.detail: The big one is on tonight. Knights are chasing their first premiership in nearly 30 years — the last time they won it all was 1997. Roosters are seasoned finals performers. Kick off 6:30pm AEST at Accor Stadium. Nothing financial here — just don't miss it.

world.summary: A busy weekend globally — US-Russia Ukraine talks take a murky turn, Trump takes aim at Canada, a US federal judge strikes down a voting law, and the Middle East conflict continues to reshape the region.

stories.title: US-Russia Ukraine talks reportedly tied to an oil deal involving Trump allies
stories.why_it_matters: Behind-the-scenes negotiations between the US and Russia over the Ukraine war are reportedly now entangled with an oil deal that benefits people connected to Trump's inner circle. The NYT reports that Trump allies stand to gain financially from any peace arrangement. This raises serious questions about whether America's Ukraine policy is being shaped by geopolitical strategy or personal financial interests — and it's exactly the kind of story that could blow up into a major political scandal. For everyday people, it matters because the Ukraine war drives European energy prices and global oil markets.

stories.title: Trump's $90 one-time payment to 20 million Medicare seniors
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has announced a one-time $90 payment to approximately 20 million Americans enrolled in Medicare (the US government's health insurance for people over 65). Critics are calling it a political handout — $90 barely covers a week's groceries — while the White House frames it as relief for seniors struggling with cost-of-living pressures. With US midterm elections approaching, the timing is being widely noted. It's a small cash splash with a large political motive.

stories.title: US federal judge rules law banning noncitizen voting is unconstitutional
stories.why_it_matters: A US federal judge has struck down a federal law that made it a crime for non-citizens to vote in US elections, ruling it unconstitutional. The judge found the law was redundant — it's already illegal for non-citizens to vote under existing law — and raised concerns about it being used to intimidate legal immigrants. The Trump administration had pushed hard for this law as part of its 'election integrity' agenda. The ruling is likely to be appealed and will be a flashpoint in the lead-up to the US midterms.

stories.title: Trump administration accuses Canada of meddling in US midterm elections
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is now pointing the finger at Canada, suggesting it is interfering in upcoming US midterm elections — without providing specific evidence. Canadian commentators are calling it scapegoating, with analyst Eric Ham arguing the consequences for the US-Canada relationship could be enormous. Canada is the US's largest trading partner; if this escalates into a diplomatic or trade dispute, it flows through to global supply chains, energy markets, and the Aussie dollar.

stories.title: Middle East: Interconnected conflicts reshape security from Yemen to Egypt
stories.why_it_matters: A new analysis highlights how the ongoing Israel-Iran conflict is sending shockwaves well beyond those two countries — Yemen's Houthi rebels are still targeting Red Sea shipping lanes, threatening global trade routes, and Egypt is being drawn deeper into regional instability. The Red Sea handles about 12% of global trade, including oil and goods shipped to Australia. Disruptions there push up shipping costs and can flow through to consumer prices here. Crude oil dropped nearly 2% last session to $91.11 — worth watching if Middle East tensions flare further.

markets.summary: A positive night on Wall Street last session, with tech leading the charge. The ASX followed suit today, closing up 0.79%. Oil slipped nearly 2% and gold eased back. The Aussie dollar ticked higher, now sitting at about 69.6 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid session today — tech and resources led the gains.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Good night last session — broad market lifted by tech.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech rally last night, with Google and Microsoft both gaining.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold eased back about 1% — still at very elevated levels historically.

indicators.name: AUD/USD

politics.summary: The RBA is front and centre this weekend — after hiking rates in September, new analysis suggests relief is still more than a year away. Treasurer Chalmers is also flagging budget pressures ahead of the mid-year update.

stories.title: RBA rate cut more than a year away, families still feeling the squeeze
stories.why_it_matters: After the RBA hiked rates again in September 2026, fresh analysis from the AFR suggests families won't see relief until well into 2028 at the earliest. That means mortgage repayments stay elevated for another year-plus, continuing to squeeze household budgets. For property owners and mortgage holders on the Gold Coast, this is a real cost — and it also means consumer spending stays under pressure, which flows into the performance of domestic-focused Aussie companies.

stories.title: Is now a good time to switch banks for a better home loan rate?
stories.why_it_matters: With the RBA having just hiked again, financial advice is circulating about whether homeowners should shop around for a better mortgage deal. The Guardian piece suggests that yes, lenders are competing aggressively for refinancers, and switching can save hundreds of dollars a month. If you're on a variable rate, it's worth spending 30 minutes comparing rates — the difference between lenders right now can be meaningful.

stories.title: Chalmers delivers ominous budget warning ahead of mid-year update
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Jim Chalmers has issued a warning that the federal budget is under more pressure than expected, ahead of the mid-year economic and fiscal outlook (MYEFO). He hasn't revealed specific numbers yet, but the language signals potential spending cuts or revised revenue forecasts. For Australians, this could mean tighter government services or adjustments to welfare payments — and it sets the political scene for a tough few months in Canberra.

ai.summary: The AI regulation debate is heating up globally — Trump is doubling down on a hands-off approach, an executive order has rebranded AI as 'Super Intelligence', and there's a fascinating benchmark battle between the top AI models.

stories.title: Trump digs in on voluntary AI safeguards as public fears grow
stories.why_it_matters: A Reuters report finds that while public anxiety about AI is growing — concerns about job losses, deep fakes, and misuse — the Trump administration is refusing to introduce mandatory safety rules. Instead, it's sticking to voluntary guidelines, meaning tech companies police themselves. This is great news for AI stocks (including your GXAI.AX ETF) because it means fewer regulatory hurdles slowing growth, but it does mean potential risks go unchecked.

stories.title: Executive Order rebrands AI as 'Super Intelligence' — and hints at federal law changes
stories.why_it_matters: A new executive order from the Trump White House has officially rebranded what we call AI as 'Super Intelligence' — a term that sounds like sci-fi but is now the official US government label. More importantly, the order signals potential changes to federal law around how AI is developed and deployed. Legal analysts at Wiley Law note this could reshape liability rules for AI companies. For investors, it's a signal that the regulatory environment is shifting — watch how Google and Microsoft respond.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Argon vs Claude Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6.1 Sol: AI model benchmark battle
stories.why_it_matters: The three biggest AI models — Google's Gemini 4 Argon, Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol — are being benchmarked head to head, with a 12-point gap reportedly separating the leaders. This is the AI equivalent of a smartphone spec war. Google (which you hold via GOOG) has a major stake in winning this race — Gemini is central to its AI strategy across Search, Cloud, and productivity tools. Staying competitive here is critical for Google's long-term value.

stories.title: PewDiePie launches Ajax: A 9 billion parameter AI model
stories.why_it_matters: In a genuinely weird development, YouTube personality PewDiePie (real name Felix Kjellberg, with 110 million subscribers) has launched his own AI model called Ajax, with 9 billion parameters — a measure of the model's size and complexity. He was apparently banned from OpenAI's tools twice before building his own. While this is more pop-culture than finance news, it illustrates just how accessible AI development has become — even individual creators are now building their own models, which signals where the technology is heading.

sport.summary: It's NRL Grand Final day — Roosters vs Knights tonight at 6:30pm AEST. The Knights are chasing their first premiership since 1997, and the storyline is enormous. AFL trade season is also heating up.

stories.title: NRL Grand Final: Roosters vs Knights — Knights chasing a 29-year fairytale
stories.why_it_matters: The 2026 NRL Grand Final is tonight — Sydney Roosters vs Newcastle Knights at Accor Stadium, 6:30pm AEST. The Knights are chasing their first premiership since 1997, nearly 30 years ago, and the storyline is enormous. Fox Sports reports a secret Roosters meeting was held during the week — suggesting some internal preparation drama — while the Knights have confirmed their fairytale charge. This is one of the biggest NRL storylines in years. Don't miss kick-off.

stories.title: This Knights premiership run is bigger than 1997 — SMH
stories.why_it_matters: The SMH argues that the Knights' 2026 finals run is actually bigger than their famous 1997 premiership because of the sheer drought since then — nearly three decades of near-misses and rebuilds. The piece is a long-form celebration of Newcastle's journey to tonight's Grand Final. For rugby league fans, especially those from Newcastle, this is the stuff of dreams. The journalist humorously notes they're refusing to speak to the Knights team for fear of jinxing it.

stories.title: AFL trade period: $18m Patrick Butters question and the mega 18-club guide
stories.why_it_matters: AFL trade period is open and the biggest question mark is Patrick Butters — valued at around $18 million — with multiple clubs reportedly circling. Fox Sports has published a comprehensive 18-club trade guide covering every club's needs and targets heading into the trade window. For AFL fans, this is the off-season soap opera — trades, delist decisions, and draft picks will reshape clubs heading into 2027.

stories.title: Koori Knockout Day 3: Results from the penultimate day
stories.why_it_matters: The Koori Knockout — one of the biggest Indigenous rugby league tournaments in the country — is into its penultimate day, with results from Day 3 now in. The tournament draws huge community participation from across NSW and Queensland, and is a major cultural event beyond just sport. Final results and the championship rounds are expected tomorrow.
